content.text: : glycoprotein manufactured through recombinant DNA technology and has the same actions as erythropoietin

: chemotherapy-induced anemia, anemia associated w/ CKD, pediatric anemia in children undergoing dialysis for CKD, reduction of allogenic blood transfusion in surgery (elective, noncardiac, nonvascular) patients at high risk for perioperative transfusion with significant, anticipated blood loss
: CKD (high BP, HA, arthralgias, nausea), HIV (fever, fatigue, HA, cough, diarrhea, rash, nausea, skin reactions, congestion, dizziness), allergic reactions
: anemia associated w/ CKD both on & off dialysis, anemia in pts w/ non-myeloid malignancies where anemia is due to the effect of concomitantly administered chemotherapy

: patients treated with ESA and dosed to a target hemoglobin concentration of 13.5 g/dL were at a significantly increased risk for serious and life-threatening CV complications (death, MI, hospitalization for CHF, stroke) compared to patients dosed to a target Hb of 11.3 g/dL – FDA recommends a target Hb in the range 10-12 g/dL and not to exceed 12 g/dL; patients have an increased risk of serious CV events and death when these products are dosed to target Hb > 12 g/dL
MOA: stim prolif & diff of RBC precursors ->↑Hgb Synth -> faster retic into blood
Endogenous EPO: nephron prod (↓nephron mass -> ↓EPO -> anemia)
Clin Use: anemia from ESA-responsive causes
Fever, HA, Myalgias                                                 -    GI effects, CP
death, MI, stroke, other serious CV events         -    Inj site pain
CKD: ↑risk death, serious adverse CV rxn, & stroke <- Hb  ±11
All hgb targets, ESA dose, or dosing strategy ↑risks
CA pt (breast, non-small cell lung, head & neck, lymphoid, cervical): ESAs shorten overall survival &/or ↑tumor progress or recurr
d/c post-chemo, ⍉ESA + myelosuppress chemotx if will cure
use lowest ESA dose to avoid RBC transfusions & serious CV/thromboembolic rxn
Rx=enroll in/comply w ESA APPRISE Oncology Program
Upper safety limits: 10 g/dL: pt ⍉dialysis, 11 g/dL: pt dialysis
Tx w ESA -> ↑iron demand SO during use of ESA tx, maintain:
All pt who receive ESA must be provided w med guide
Monitoring:      -    Hgb     -    Serum ferritin       -    Transferrin sat       -    BP
Clin Use: Pre-op: DVT prophylaxis when used

content.text: Administration: empty stomach if tolerate, goal =200 mg elemental iron/day
If w food ->  w Vit C OR tomato juice -> ↑absorb & ↓GI effects
If ⍉tolerate PO -> iron fortified foods (cereals) or parenteral iron
Adverse Effects: GI: Epigastric pain, N/V/D/C, melena
Accidental overdose= leading cause of peds (<6 y/o) fatal poisoning
Store out peds reach. overdose =immediately call doctor or poison control
↓absorb: thyroid meds, some abx (tetracycline, fluoroquinolone) & vit E
Monitoring:    -   Hgb/HCT     -   Iron studies: Ferritin, Serum Fe, Transferrin sat
Non-responsive pt -> compliance/absorb issue? cont blood loss? alt dx?
